$comment: Copy to journey-qa.config.json and edit. NEVER commit real passwords — keep them in .env (TEST_PASSWORD) and reference env where possible. This file is safe to commit only with placeholder/non-secret values.
$comment_urls: base_url = public/app host. admin_base_url = where the admin panel lives (often the same host, sometimes a separate subdomain). Override at runtime with JOURNEY_BASE / JOURNEY_ADMIN_BASE env vars.
$comment_lang: UI language of the target app. Used to pick the right button-label dictionary below.

labels.$comment: Visible button/link text the runner looks for, by intent. Add your app's wording (any language). Regex, case-insensitive. The blind MCP tester reads these too but still navigates by what it actually sees.

auth.$comment_login_path: Relative path of the login form.
auth.$comment_two_step: true if the form asks for email first, then password on a second screen.
auth.$comment_success: After a successful login the URL pathname should no longer match this (used to detect login success/failure).

fixtures.$comment: Abstract user archetypes → the credentials the runner/agent will use. Emails are placeholders; the PASSWORD comes from env TEST_PASSWORD (do not hardcode secrets). 'anonymous' needs no entry. Map only the archetypes your journeys actually use.

verified_user.note: fully onboarded user who can perform core actions

staff_limited.note: internal staff with a narrow permission set
